5. This Court has noticed with a great degree of concem that in a good number of cases, trials have remained pending well beyond the statutory period, so prescribed by the law. Such delays not only erode public confidence in the administration ofjustice but also stand in direct contravention of the fundamental principles of fair trial and timely adjudication, which form the bedrock ofour legal system' The failure to conclude trials within the prescribed period adversely affects the rights of all stakeholders, particularly the \-> accused persons, who are presumed innocent until proven guilty, and the victims, who await closure and redress.

At this juncture, this court must say that, despite the existence of a well-structured framework for the expeditious disposal of cases, as provided in the National Judicial Policy, 2009, still the rate of disposal of criminal cases remains discouragingly low. In many instances, the proceedings continue to progress at an unacceptably slow pace, akin to a snail's crawl, thereby defeating the very spirit of timely justice and undermining public confidence in the efficiency of the criminal justice system. The purpose and intent behind the aforesaid reproduction was to underscore and draw the attention of all ,:.\ the stakeholders viz. subordinate courts, members of the legal fraternity, officers / officials ofjustice sector and the litigants to the prevailing issues insofar as nondisposal of cases within the stipulated period is concemed. It serves as a reminder of their shared responsibility in ensuring the timely dispensation of justice and to highlight the need for greater diligence, commitnenq and adherence to judicid norms and timelines. All the courts, subordinate to the High Court, across the province are supposed to ensure strict compliance with the guidelines laid down in the National Judicial Policy, 2009 because adherence to these directives is essential for securing the timely and effective disposal of criminal cases within the prescribed periods.
